records.source: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ· Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.
records.gloss: And going out of him out of the temple says to him one of the disciples of him, Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!
pieces: Jesus was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way out of the temple when one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples exclaimed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look! Such stones! Such buildings!"

L.1: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out of the temple, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!"

R.1: Jesus was walking out of the temple courts. One of the disciples called out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look at these huge stones! Look at these wonderful buildings!"

decisions.choice: says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, a past event is told in the present tense to make it vivid. The sense is past: he said.

decisions.choice: what stones, what buildings: an exclamation of wonder at their size and splendor
alternatives: a question about what kind of stones they were
decisions.reason: The word asks "of what sort", and here it marks amazement: what great stones, what fine buildings.

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts, rebuilt on a grand scale by Herod the Great
decisions.reason: Herod began rebuilding the temple about 20 BC, and work went on for decades. Some of its stones were enormous; blocks from the retaining walls can still be seen in Jerusalem. The word used here covers the whole complex, not only the sanctuary building.

decisions.choice: temple courts; huge stones; wonderful buildings
alternatives: the temple; what stones and what buildings
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus left the temple area and spells out what the disciple was admiring.

records.heading: Not one stone left on another

records.source: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς;
records.gloss: And Jesus said to him, See you these great buildings?
pieces: Jesus replied, "You see these great buildings?

L.2: And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings?

R.2: Jesus answered, "Do you see these big buildings?

decisions.choice: Do you see these great buildings? a question that turns the disciple's wonder toward what will happen to them
alternatives: a statement: you see these great buildings
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a question or as a statement. Either way Jesus takes up the disciple's admiration and answers it with a warning.

decisions.choice: said to him: to the one disciple who spoke
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular. The answer is given to the disciple who spoke, though the others hear it.

decisions.choice: You see these great buildings?
alternatives: Do you see these great buildings?
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the question in the form of spoken English, with the voice rising at the end.

records.source: οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.
records.gloss: No not shall be left here stone upon stone which no not shall be thrown down.
pieces: Not one stone here will be left resting on another. Every one will be pulled down."

L.2: There will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down."

R.2: Every one of them will be torn down. Not a single stone will be left on top of another."

decisions.choice: will not, will not: two double negatives, a strong and certain prediction
decisions.reason: Each "no not" in the Greek is the strongest way of denying something. Jesus says the destruction will certainly be complete.

decisions.choice: be thrown down: a passive, the one who destroys is not named
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull down or demolish. The passive leaves the destroyer unnamed.

decisions.choice: the prediction of the temple's destruction
decisions.reason: Roman forces destroyed the temple in AD 70, when they took Jerusalem. Prophets had spoken in the same way about the first temple (Micah 3:12; Jeremiah 7:14; 26:18).

decisions.choice: Every one of them will be torn down. Not a single stone ...
alternatives: Not a stone will be left upon a stone that will not be thrown down
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main point first and then the picture of the stones, in two short sentences.

records.source: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀνδρέας·
records.gloss: And sitting of him on the Mount of the Olives opposite the temple were asking him privately Peter and James and John and Andrew:
pieces: Then, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on the Mount of Olives facing the temple, four of them, Peter, James, John and Andrew, put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in private:

L.3: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately:

R.3: Later Jesus sat down on the Mount of Olives. From there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could see the temple across the valley. Peter, James, John, and Andrew came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a question:

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives opposite the temple: the ridge east of Jerusalem, looking down on the temple across the Kidron Valley
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives rises higher than the temple mount and faces it across a narrow valley. From there the whole temple could be seen.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: perhaps recalling the prophecy of the Lord standing there on the day of judgment
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 says that on the day of the Lord his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives. Jesus' speech about the end is given on that same hill. Mark does not draw the link himself.

decisions.choice: privately: the four alone, apart from the others
decisions.reason: As in 4:34 and 9:28, the private setting marks teaching meant for the disciples. The four named are the first four called (1:16-20).

decisions.choice: From there he could see the temple across the valley; came to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "opposite" means here and says the four came to Jesus on their own.

records.source: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα.
records.gloss: Tell us, when these things will be, and what the sign when are about these things to be accomplished all?
pieces: "Tell us, when will these things take place? And what sign will there be when all of them are about to reach their completion?"

L.4: "Tell us, when will these things be, and what [will be] the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?"

R.4: "Tell us, when will this happen? What sign will show us that all these things are about to be completed?"

decisions.choice: these things: the destruction of the temple Jesus has just foretold
alternatives: the end of the world in general
decisions.reason: The question picks up Jesus' words in 13:2. In the second half, "all these things" widens it to everything that goes with that event.

decisions.choice: be accomplished: be brought to completion, reach their end
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to an end or to complete. It suggests that the disciples link the temple's fall with the close of the age.

decisions.choice: all these things ... be completed: perhaps echoing Daniel 12:7
decisions.reason: In Daniel 12:7 the angel says that when the power of the holy people is shattered, all these things will be completed. The disciples' words sound much the same.

decisions.choice: two questions: when, and what sign
decisions.reason: The disciples ask when, and how they will know it is near. The speech answers the second question at length and says in 13:32 that no one knows the day.

decisions.choice: reach their completion (B); be completed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for coming to an end.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
records.gloss: And Jesus began to say to them, Take heed lest anyone you mislead.
pieces: Jesus began to speak to them: "Be on your guard, so that nobody leads you astray.

L.5: And Jesus began to say to them, "Take care that no one misleads you.

R.5: Jesus began to answer them. "Be careful! Do not let anyone fool you.

decisions.choice: began to say: the start of a long speech that runs to the end of the chapter (13:37)
decisions.reason: This is the longest speech of Jesus in Mark. Everything to 13:37 is his answer to the four.

decisions.choice: take heed: look out, be on guard
decisions.reason: The verb is "see", used as a warning. It returns at 13:9, 13:23 and 13:33 and holds the speech together.

decisions.choice: mislead: lead astray, deceive
decisions.reason: The word means to make someone wander from the right way. The first danger Jesus names is deception, not suffering.

decisions.choice: take care (L); be on your guard (B); be careful (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the same English for this warning wherever it returns in the speech.

records.source: πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
records.gloss: Many will come in the name of me saying that I am, and many they will mislead.
pieces: Many will come using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and saying, 'I am he,' and they will lead many astray.

L.6: Many will come in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, 'I am [he],' and they will mislead many.

R.6: Many people will come and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. They will say, 'I am the one!' They will fool many people.

decisions.choice: in my name: claiming my title or my authority
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to come claiming to act for them, or to be them. These people take for themselves what belongs to Jesus.

decisions.choice: I am: I am the one, the expected deliverer
alternatives: it is I, Jesus, come back
decisions.reason: The two words stand without anything after them. They mean "I am he": the one people are waiting for. Some read them as a claim to be Jesus himself returned.

decisions.choice: I am: the words Jesus himself uses at 6:50 and 14:62, which recall God's name in Exodus 3:14
decisions.reason: On Jesus' lips these words carry great weight. The deceivers will take them for themselves.

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); I am he (B); I am the one (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a word after "I am". Literal brackets it; Readable makes the claim plain.

records.source: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλ’ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: When then you hear of wars and reports of wars, not be alarmed; it must happen, but not yet the end.
pieces: When you hear of wars, and news of wars far away, do not be shaken. These things have to come, but that is not yet the end.

L.7: And when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; it must happen, but the end [is] not yet.

R.7: You will hear about wars close by and news of wars far away. Do not be afraid. These things must happen, but the end has not come yet.

decisions.choice: reports of wars: news of wars elsewhere
decisions.reason: Wars nearby are heard; wars far off are heard about. The phrase covers both.

decisions.choice: it must happen: part of what God has planned
alternatives: it is bound to happen by chance
decisions.reason: "Must" here expresses God's purpose, as in Daniel 2:28: what must happen in the last days.

decisions.choice: the end: the end of the age
decisions.reason: War is not the signal that the end has come. The same word returns in 13:13.

decisions.choice: wars ... news of wars far away (B); wars close by and news of wars far away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the second phrase means instead of keeping the old pairing.

records.source: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ἔσονται λιμοί· ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.
records.gloss: Will rise up for nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, there will be earthquakes in places, there will be famines; beginning of birth pains these.
pieces: Nation will go to war against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. Earthquakes will strike in one place after another, and there will be famines. All this is only the first of the birth pains.

L.8: For nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in [various] places; there will be famines. These [are the] beginning of birth pains.

R.8: Nations will fight against each other, and kingdoms will attack other kingdoms. There will be earthquakes in many places, and people will go hungry. But all this is only the start of the pain. It is like the first pains of a woman giving birth.

decisions.choice: nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom: in the words of Isaiah 19:2
decisions.reason: Isaiah 19:2 speaks of city against city and kingdom against kingdom, in God's judgment on Egypt. Jesus uses the prophets' language for the troubles ahead.

decisions.choice: the beginning of birth pains: the first of the sufferings that come before God's new age
alternatives: the start of the end itself
decisions.reason: The prophets used a woman's labor as a picture of the distress that comes before God acts (Isaiah 26:17-19; Micah 4:9-10). Birth pains are hard but lead to new life, and these are only the first of them.

decisions.choice: in places: here and there, in one place after another
decisions.reason: The phrase means throughout different places.

decisions.choice: there will be famines: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and troubles" after famines, a natural addition to the list. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: It is like the first pains of a woman giving birth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of birth pains.

records.source: βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Take heed however you to yourselves; they will deliver up you to councils and in synagogues you will be beaten and before governors and kings you will stand because of me for a testimony to them.
pieces: As for you, be on your guard. People will hand you over to the councils, and you will be flogged in the synagogues. You will stand before governors and kings for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, to bear witness to them.

L.9: But you, take care for yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and in synagogues you will be beaten, and before governors and kings you will stand because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as a testimony to them.

R.9: Be careful about what will happen to you. People will take you to court. They will beat you in their meeting places. You will be put on trial in front of governors and kings because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That way you will be able to tell them about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: they will hand over: the same verb used of John (1:14) and of Jesus himself (9:31; 10:33)
decisions.reason: The disciples will go the way their teacher goes: handed over to the authorities.

decisions.choice: councils, synagogues, beaten: local Jewish courts and the floggings they could order
decisions.reason: Local councils judged cases, and a synagogue could punish with a flogging of up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:2-3). Paul received thirty-nine lashes five times (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: in synagogues you will be beaten: a new clause
alternatives: they will hand you over to councils and to synagogues; you will be beaten
decisions.reason: The phrase "in synagogues" could be joined to "hand over". The SBLGNT punctuation and the word order favor taking it with "you will be beaten".

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: to bear witness about Jesus before them
decisions.reason: The same phrase in 6:11 means evidence against people. Here, before rulers and kings, it most likely means that the disciples' trials will give them a chance to speak about Jesus (compare 13:10).

decisions.choice: take you to court; meeting places; because you follow me; tell them about me
alternatives: councils; synagogues; because of me; as a testimony to them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the councils and synagogues and says what the testimony means. "Tell them about me" follows the reading chosen above.

records.source: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πρῶτον δεῖ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
records.gloss: And to all the nations first must be proclaimed the gospel.
pieces: And first the gospel has to be proclaimed to all the nations.

L.10: And to all the nations the gospel must first be proclaimed.

R.10: Before the end comes, the good news must be told to people of every nation.

decisions.choice: first: before the end of 13:7
decisions.reason: "First" looks back to "not yet the end". The gospel will go to the nations before the end comes.

decisions.choice: must: God's plan, as in 13:7
decisions.reason: The same word as in 13:7. The spread of the gospel is part of what God has planned.

decisions.choice: to all the nations: begins a new sentence
alternatives: joined to 13:9: as a testimony to them and to all the nations
decisions.reason: Some read "to all the nations" with the end of 13:9. The SBLGNT begins a new sentence with it, and the word order supports that.

decisions.choice: Before the end comes
decisions.reason: Readable says what "first" is first to.

records.source: καὶ ὅταν ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί λαλήσητε, ἀλλ’ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦτο λαλεῖτε, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.
records.gloss: And when they lead you, handing over, not be anxious beforehand what you should say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, this speak; not for are you those speaking but the Spirit the Holy.
pieces: When they take you away to hand you over, do not be anxious in advance about what you will say. Whatever words are given to you in that hour, speak them. It will not be you who are speaking. It will be the Holy Spirit.

L.11: And when they lead you [away], handing [you] over, do not be anxious beforehand about what you will say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

R.11: When you are arrested and put on trial, do not worry before it happens about what you will say. When the time comes, God will give you the words. Say what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives you. You will not be the one speaking. The Holy Spirit will speak through you.

decisions.choice: is given: a passive, God is the giver
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. The end of the verse names the Holy Spirit as the one who speaks.

decisions.choice: in that hour: at that moment, when you are on trial
decisions.reason: "Hour" here means the time when something happens.

decisions.choice: the Spirit speaking for them: like God's promise to Moses
decisions.reason: When Moses feared to speak before Pharaoh, God promised to be with his mouth and teach him what to say (Exodus 4:12).

decisions.choice: arrested and put on trial; God will give you the words
alternatives: they lead you away, handing you over; is given
decisions.reason: Readable says what being led away and handed over means and names God as the giver.

records.source: καὶ παραδώσει ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·
records.gloss: And will deliver up brother brother to death and father child, and will rise up children against parents and will put to death them.
pieces: Brothers will hand their brothers over to be killed, and fathers their children. Children will rise up against their parents and send them to their deaths.

L.12: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father [his] child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

R.12: Families will turn against each other. Brothers will hand their own brothers over to be killed. Fathers will do this to their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them killed.

decisions.choice: children against parents: in the words of Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Micah 7:6 describes a time when a son treats his father with contempt and a daughter rises against her mother, and a person's enemies are in their own household.

decisions.choice: put them to death: cause them to be executed, by handing them over to the authorities
alternatives: kill them with their own hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring about someone's death. In context it means betraying them to the courts.

decisions.choice: will hand over: the same verb as in 13:9 and 13:11
decisions.reason: The handing over now comes from inside the family.

decisions.choice: Families will turn against each other.
decisions.reason: Readable begins with a short sentence that says what the verse describes.

records.source: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
records.gloss: And you will be hated by all because of the name of me.
pieces: Everyone will hate you because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.13: And you will be hated by all because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

R.13: Everyone will hate you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you bear my name and belong to me
alternatives: because you speak my name aloud
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. They will be hated for being known as Jesus' followers.

decisions.choice: by all: by people everywhere
decisions.reason: "All" is a strong general word: they will meet hatred on every side.

decisions.choice: because you belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my name" means here.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
records.gloss: The however having endured to end this will be saved.
pieces: But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.

L.13: But the one who has endured to [the] end, this one will be saved.

R.13: But those who do not give up, right to the end, will be saved.

decisions.choice: endured: held out, stayed faithful under pressure
decisions.reason: The verb means to remain under a burden without giving way. Here it means staying loyal to Jesus while hated and handed over.

decisions.choice: to the end: to the very end, whether of one's life or of the time of trouble
alternatives: to the end of the age only
decisions.reason: There is no article, and the phrase can mean completely, to the last. It may also look back to "the end" in 13:7.

decisions.choice: will be saved: final salvation by God, not escape from death
decisions.reason: Some of these believers will be put to death (13:12). The promise is that God will save them in the end.

decisions.choice: whoever holds out (B); those who do not give up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for enduring. The Greek speaks of anyone, so no male form is needed.

records.source: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω τι ἆραι ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: When then you see the abomination of the desolation standing where not it must, the one reading let him understand, then those in Judea let them flee to the mountains, \v 15 the one upon the housetop not let him come down nor go in anything to take out of the house of him, \v 16 and the one in the field not let him return to the things behind to take the cloak of him.
pieces: But when you see the abomination that brings ruin standing where he has no right to be (let the reader take note), then those who are in Judea must escape to the hills.
Anyone who is on the roof must not go down into the house to fetch anything out of it.
Anyone who is out in the field must not go back for a cloak.

L.14: But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where he must not (let the one reading understand), then let those in Judea flee to the mountains;
L.15: let the one on the housetop not come down nor go in to take anything out of {{gender:their|his}} house,
L.16: and let the one in the field not turn back to the things behind to take {{gender:their|his}} cloak.

R.14: One day you will see 'the horrible thing that destroys' standing where he should not stand. (Reader, think carefully about what this means.) When that happens, people in Judea must run away to the hills.
R.15: If someone is up on the roof of a house, they must not go down and go inside to get anything.
R.16: If someone is working in the field, they must not go back to get their coat.

decisions.choice: the abomination of desolation: the phrase from Daniel 9:27, 11:31 and 12:11
decisions.reason: In Daniel it is a detestable thing set up in God's sanctuary that leaves it desolate. In 167 BC the Syrian king Antiochus IV set up a pagan altar on the temple altar, and 1 Maccabees 1:54 uses the same phrase for it. Jesus says something like it will happen again.

decisions.choice: standing: a masculine participle, pointing to a person
alternatives: it standing: a thing, matching the noun
decisions.reason: The noun "abomination" is neuter, but "standing" is masculine. That suggests a person: someone who stands where only God belongs. Mark does not say who.

decisions.choice: where he must not: in the holy place, the temple
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of the sanctuary, and Matthew 24:15 says "in the holy place". Mark keeps the phrase veiled.

decisions.choice: let the one reading understand: an aside to the reader
alternatives: Jesus telling his hearers to read Daniel carefully
decisions.reason: The words speak of reading, not hearing, so they are most likely Mark's own words to those who read his book aloud or to themselves. They urge the reader to see what the veiled phrase means.

decisions.choice: the housetop, the cloak: flat roofs used as living space, and the outer garment laid aside for work
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by an outside stair, so one could leave without going in. A worker in the field would lay the outer cloak aside. The danger will be so sudden that there is no time even for these.

decisions.choice: their or his (L); anyone ... a cloak (B); someone ... they (R)
alternatives: let him ... his house ... his cloak
decisions.reason: The commands are general and apply to anyone. Literal offers "their" or "his" through the gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "anyone" and "they".

decisions.choice: the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that destroys (R); let the reader take note (B); Reader, think carefully about what this means (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Daniel's phrase as it is. Balanced and Readable say what it means. All levels keep Mark's aside in parentheses.

records.heading: When you see the abomination

records.source: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
records.gloss: Woe then to those in womb having and to those nursing in those days.
pieces: How terrible it will be in those days for women who are expecting a child or nursing a baby!

L.17: And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!

R.17: Those days will be very hard for women who are going to have a baby, and for mothers who are feeding babies.

decisions.choice: having in the womb: pregnant
decisions.reason: "To have in the womb" is the ordinary Greek way of saying a woman is pregnant.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and pity
decisions.reason: Here "woe" is not a curse on these women. It grieves for them, because they will find it hardest to flee.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be (B); will be very hard (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the cry of pity in current English.

records.source: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται χειμῶνος·
records.gloss: Pray then that not it happen in winter.
pieces: Pray that this does not come in winter.

L.18: And pray that it may not happen in winter.

R.18: Pray that it will not happen in the winter.

decisions.choice: winter: the cold, rainy season
decisions.reason: In Judea winter is the rainy season. Streams in the valleys run high and roads turn to mud, so flight on foot would be hard.

decisions.choice: it: the time of flight and trouble just described
decisions.reason: There is no stated subject. The sense is that the time of flight should not fall in winter.

decisions.choice: that it not happen in winter: the SBLGNT reading
alternatives: that your flight not happen in winter
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "your flight", as in Matthew 24:20, making the subject clear. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

records.source: ἔσονται γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι θλῖψις οἵα οὐ γέγονεν τοιαύτη ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἣν ἔκτισεν ὁ θεὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν καὶ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
records.gloss: Will be for the days those tribulation such as not has happened such from beginning of creation which created God until the now and no not will happen.
pieces: For those days will bring distress unlike any there has been from the beginning, when God created the world, until now, or ever will be again.

L.19: For those days will be tribulation such as has not happened from [the] beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will.

R.19: That will be a time of terrible trouble. Nothing like it has happened since God made the world, and nothing like it will ever happen again.

decisions.choice: tribulation such as has not happened: in the words of Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:1 speaks of a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation until that time. Jesus widens it to the whole of creation.

decisions.choice: those days will be tribulation: those days will be a time of great distress
decisions.reason: The days are described as being the distress itself, a strong way of saying what will fill them.

decisions.choice: the creation which God created: a doubled phrase that stresses the whole span of time
decisions.reason: Saying the same thing twice is a Hebrew way of adding weight: since the very beginning of everything God made.

decisions.choice: never will: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strong denial again: there will never be another time like it.

decisions.choice: tribulation (L); distress (B); terrible trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long-used word. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for great suffering and pressure.

records.source: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολόβωσεν κύριος τὰς ἡμέρας, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ.
records.gloss: And if not had shortened Lord the days, not would have been saved any flesh.
pieces: If the Lord had not cut those days short, no one at all would survive.

L.20: And if [the] Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved.

R.20: If the Lord had not made that time shorter, no one would live through it.

decisions.choice: Lord: God
decisions.reason: Here "Lord" means God, as the next sentence shows: the one who chose the elect.

decisions.choice: any flesh: any human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for living people. "No flesh" means no one.

decisions.choice: be saved: survive, come through alive
decisions.reason: Here the word speaks of living through the distress, not of salvation at the end as in 13:13.

decisions.choice: had shortened: the past tense speaks of a decision God has already made
decisions.reason: The days have not yet come, but God has already decided to cut them short.

decisions.choice: survive (B); live through it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that physical survival is meant.

records.source: ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἐκολόβωσεν τὰς ἡμέρας.
records.gloss: But because of the elect whom he chose he shortened the days.
pieces: But because of the chosen, those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cut the days short.

L.20: But because of the elect, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shortened the days.

R.20: But God has chosen people to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. For their sake {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made that time shorter.

decisions.choice: the elect: the people God has chosen, his people
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the chosen are God's people. Here they are those who belong to God through Jesus (13:22, 27).

decisions.choice: chose: a middle form, chose for himself
decisions.reason: The form stresses that God chose them to be his own.

decisions.choice: the elect whom he chose: a doubled phrase that stresses God's choice
decisions.reason: As in 13:19, the repeated root adds weight.

decisions.choice: God has chosen people to be his own
alternatives: because of the elect whom he chose
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what "the elect" means.

records.source: καὶ τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἴδε ὧδε ὁ χριστός, Ἴδε ἐκεῖ, μὴ πιστεύετε·
records.gloss: And then if anyone to you says, Look, here the Christ, look, there, not believe.
pieces: At that time, if anyone tells you, 'See, here is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!' or 'See, there he is!' do not believe it.

L.21: And then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},' 'Look, there,' do not believe [it].

R.21: At that time someone may say to you, 'Look, here is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!' or 'Look, he is over there!' Do not believe it.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: "Christ" is the Greek for the Hebrew title Messiah, the Anointed One. People will claim the promised king has appeared.

decisions.choice: then: in that time of distress
decisions.reason: "Then" ties the warning to the days just described.

decisions.choice: do not believe: a present command, do not go on believing such claims
alternatives: do not listen to them at all
decisions.reason: The command is plain: refuse to believe such reports, however often they come.

decisions.choice: 'Look, there' (L); 'See, there he is!' (B); 'Look, he is over there!' (R)
decisions.reason: Greek gives only "look, there". Balanced and Readable add "or" and "he is" to make the second claim a full saying.

records.source: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πρὸς τὸ ἀποπλανᾶν εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
records.gloss: Will arise for false-christs and false-prophets and will give signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, the elect.
pieces: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will rise up and do signs and wonders, so as to lead the chosen ones astray, if that could be done.

L.22: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, the elect.

R.22: People will come who falsely claim to be {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Others will falsely claim to be prophets. They will do signs and amazing things to fool God's chosen people, if they can.

decisions.choice: false christs: people who falsely claim to be the Messiah
decisions.reason: The word joins "false" and "Christ". It means pretenders to the title of Messiah.

decisions.choice: false prophets with signs and wonders: as in Deuteronomy 13:1-3
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:1-3 warns that a prophet may give a sign or wonder that comes true and still lead people after other gods. Signs alone do not prove a messenger is from God.

decisions.choice: if possible: they will try, though it may not be possible
decisions.reason: The phrase shows how strong the deception will be. It also hints that God will keep his chosen ones from being led away.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: works that seem to show power from God
decisions.reason: The pair is the Old Testament phrase for God's mighty acts, as in Egypt (Deuteronomy 6:22).

decisions.choice: who falsely claim to be the Messiah; God's chosen people
alternatives: false Christs, false prophets; the elect
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two compound words mean and whose chosen people they are.

records.source: ὑμεῖς δὲ βλέπετε· προείρηκα ὑμῖν πάντα.
records.gloss: You however take heed; I have foretold to you all things.
pieces: So you must be on your guard. I have told you all of it in advance.

L.23: But you, take care; I have told you all things beforehand.

R.23: So be careful! I have warned you about all this before it happens.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, you as opposed to those who are misled
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis: whatever others do, you be on guard.

decisions.choice: all things: everything they need to know about these events
decisions.reason: Jesus has told them all they need to keep from being deceived, not every detail of what will happen.

decisions.choice: warned you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the telling is for.

records.source: Ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν ἐκείνην ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες ἔσονται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πίπτοντες, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς σαλευθήσονται.
records.gloss: But in those days after the tribulation that the sun will be darkened, and the moon not will give the light of it, \v 25 and the stars will be out of the heaven falling, and the powers that in the heavens will be shaken.
pieces: But in those days, after that time of distress, the sun will grow dark and the moon will give no light.
Stars will come falling from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.

L.24: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,
L.25: and the stars will be falling out of heaven, and the powers that [are] in the heavens will be shaken.

R.24: In those days, after that time of terrible trouble, the sun will become dark. The moon will not shine.
R.25: Stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the heavens will be shaken.

decisions.choice: sun, moon and stars: in the words of Isaiah 13:10 and 34:4
alternatives: a new prophecy with no source
decisions.reason: Isaiah 13:10 says the sun will be dark and the moon will not give its light; Isaiah 34:4 says the host of heaven will fall. Joel 2:10 and 3:15 speak the same way.

decisions.choice: darkened sun and falling stars: the prophets' language for God acting in judgment
alternatives: only a description of the physical sky
decisions.reason: Isaiah used these words about the fall of Babylon (Isaiah 13). Such language marks a great act of God that shakes the world. How literally it is meant here is not certain.

decisions.choice: the powers in the heavens: the heavenly bodies, or spiritual powers ruling there
decisions.reason: "Powers" can mean the sun, moon and stars as the host of heaven, or spiritual beings. Both were thought of together.

decisions.choice: in those days, after that tribulation: a new stage after the distress of 13:14-23
alternatives: the same moment as the distress
decisions.reason: "But" and "after" mark a turn from the troubles to what follows them.

decisions.choice: sky
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means both sky and heaven. Where stars fall, Balanced and Readable say sky.

records.heading: The Son of Man coming in the clouds

records.source: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλαις μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης·
records.gloss: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with power great and glory.
pieces: Then people will see the Son of Man come in clouds, with great power and glory.

L.26: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

R.26: Then everyone will see the Son of Man come in the clouds. He will come with great power and glory.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in clouds: Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given authority and a kingdom that will never end. Jesus uses the title of himself throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: coming: the Son of Man coming in glory at the end
alternatives: only his going up to God to be crowned
decisions.reason: In Daniel the son of man comes to the Ancient of Days. Some read Jesus' words as his going to God in triumph. The angels gathering the elect in 13:27 point to his coming to earth.

decisions.choice: they will see: people in general
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It means people will see.

decisions.choice: people (B); everyone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

records.source: καὶ τότε ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἐπισυνάξει τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρου γῆς ἕως ἄκρου οὐρανοῦ.
records.gloss: And then he will send the angels and will gather together the elect from the four winds from end of earth to end of heaven.
pieces: And then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels and gather the chosen ones from all four winds, from the farthest edge of the earth to the farthest edge of the sky.

L.27: And then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels and will gather together the elect from the four winds, from [the] end of earth to [the] end of heaven.

R.27: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels. They will gather God's chosen people from every direction, from one end of the earth and sky to the other.

decisions.choice: gathering the elect from the four winds: as God promised to gather his scattered people
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 30:4 promises to gather Israel even from the end of heaven, and Zechariah 2:6 speaks of the four winds. Now the Son of Man gathers the chosen.

decisions.choice: the four winds: the four directions, everywhere
decisions.reason: The four winds are north, south, east and west.

decisions.choice: from the end of earth to the end of heaven: from every corner of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase joins two Old Testament ways of saying "everywhere": the ends of the earth and the ends of the sky, where they seem to meet.

decisions.choice: the angels, the elect: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "his angels" and "his elect", as in Matthew 24:31. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: God's chosen people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose chosen people they are, as in 13:20.

records.source: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς ἁπαλὸς γένηται καὶ ἐκφύῃ τὰ φύλλα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
records.gloss: From now the fig tree learn the parable: when already the branch of it tender becomes and puts out the leaves, you know that near the summer is.
pieces: Learn this parable from the fig tree. Once its branch turns soft and its leaves sprout, you know summer is close.

L.28: Now from the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out the leaves, you know that the summer is near.

R.28: Learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches get soft and green and new leaves begin to grow, you know that summer will soon be here.

decisions.choice: the fig tree's leaves: a sign of summer
decisions.reason: Most trees in the land of Israel keep their leaves all year. The fig loses its leaves in winter, and new ones come late in spring, so its leaves are a sure sign that summer is near.

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison that teaches a lesson
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short comparison from nature.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: perhaps recalling the fig tree of 11:12-14 and 11:20-21
decisions.reason: Earlier a fig tree without fruit stood for judgment. Here the fig tree's new leaves show that something is near.

decisions.choice: lesson
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Readable avoids "parable". Here the word means the lesson the fig tree teaches.

records.heading: Learn from the fig tree

records.source: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.
records.gloss: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that near it is at doors.
pieces: So too with you: when you see these things happening, be sure that it is near, right at the door.

L.29: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that [it] is near, at [the] doors.

R.29: In the same way, when you see these things happening, you can be sure that the time is near. It is right at the door.

decisions.choice: is near: the subject is not stated; the end, or the coming of the Son of Man
alternatives: he is near: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject, so it can mean "it is near" or "he is near". Luke 21:31 says "the kingdom of God is near". The coming of the Son of Man in 13:26 is what is near in either reading.

decisions.choice: these things: the troubles and signs of 13:5-23
alternatives: the darkening of the sun and the coming itself
decisions.reason: "These things" are what come before the end, as in the disciples' question (13:4).

decisions.choice: know: a command
decisions.reason: The same form can be a command or a statement. After "so also you" it is most likely a command.

decisions.choice: at the doors: very close
alternatives: at the doors of the temple
decisions.reason: To be at the door is to be about to come in.

decisions.choice: the time is near
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject as the time of these events, which keeps both readings open as far as English allows.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη μέχρις οὗ ταῦτα πάντα γένηται.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that no not will pass away the generation this until these things all have taken place.
pieces: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away before all these things take place.

L.30: Truly I say to you that this generation will not pass away until all these things have taken place.

R.30: I tell you the truth: all these things will happen before the people now living have all died.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living in Jesus' own time
alternatives: the generation that sees the signs
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Mark "this generation" means Jesus' contemporaries (8:12, 38; 9:19). Others take it as the people of Israel or the generation alive when the signs begin. The meaning depends on what "all these things" includes.

decisions.choice: all these things: the events of 13:5-23, including the fall of the temple
alternatives: everything in the speech, including the coming of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: "These things" in 13:29 are the signs that come before the end. Read that way, Jesus says his own generation will see them, while the day itself no one knows (13:32).

decisions.choice: will not: a double negative, a firm promise
decisions.reason: The strongest form of denial.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as elsewhere in Mark.

decisions.choice: the people now living
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading chosen above. If it is wrong, this wording says more than the Greek.

records.source: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
records.gloss: The heaven and the earth will pass away, but the words of me no not will pass away.
pieces: Heaven and earth will pass away, yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will never pass away.

L.31: Heaven and earth will pass away, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will by no means pass away.

R.31: The sky and the earth will come to an end, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will last forever.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth pass, my words remain: as God's word stands forever
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40:8 says the word of our God stands forever, and Isaiah 51:6 says the heavens will vanish like smoke. Jesus says of his own words what the prophets said of God's word.

decisions.choice: will by no means pass away: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strongest denial: his words will never fail.

decisions.choice: come to an end; last forever
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for passing away and never passing away.

records.source: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἢ τῆς ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι ἐν οὐρανῷ οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ.
records.gloss: Concerning now the day that or the hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven nor the Son, except the Father.
pieces: As for that day or hour, nobody knows it, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son. Only the Father knows.

L.32: But concerning that day or the hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, except the Father.

R.32: But no one knows the day or the hour when this will happen. The angels in heaven do not know. Even the Son does not know. Only the Father knows.

decisions.choice: that day: the day of the Son of Man's coming (13:26)
alternatives: the day of the temple's fall
decisions.reason: "That day" is the prophets' phrase for the day of the Lord. Here it is the day of the coming just described.

decisions.choice: nor the Son: Jesus says that he, the Son, does not know the day
alternatives: the Son knows but will not tell
decisions.reason: Mark records this plainly. The Son shares the life of the Father, yet as he lives among people he does not know the day; the Father alone has set it. The text does not explain this further.

decisions.choice: the Son, the Father: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of God the Father
decisions.reason: Only here in Mark does Jesus call himself simply "the Son" beside "the Father".

decisions.choice: when this will happen; Even the Son does not know
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the list into short sentences and says what the day is.

records.heading: Keep awake

records.source: βλέπετε ἀγρυπνεῖτε, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ καιρός ἐστιν·
records.gloss: Take heed, keep awake; not you know for when the time is.
pieces: Be on your guard and stay alert, because you do not know when the time will come.

L.33: Take care, stay awake; for you do not know when the time is.

R.33: So be careful! Stay awake! You do not know when that time will come.

decisions.choice: keep awake: stay alert, do not fall asleep
decisions.reason: The verb means to be sleepless. It means watching and being ready.

decisions.choice: the time: the appointed time, the moment God has set
decisions.reason: This word for time often means a fixed or decisive moment.

decisions.choice: stay awake: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and pray", perhaps from 14:38. Some important early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: stay alert
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word that covers both keeping awake and being ready.

records.source: ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀπόδημος ἀφεὶς τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ δοὺς τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐξουσίαν, ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῷ θυρωρῷ ἐνετείλατο ἵνα γρηγορῇ.
records.gloss: Like a man away from home, having left the house of him and having given to the slaves of him the authority, to each the work of him, and the doorkeeper he commanded that he keep watch.
pieces: It is like a man who goes away from home. He leaves his house, puts his servants in charge, each with a task to do, and orders the doorkeeper to keep watch.

L.34: [It is] like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave his slaves the authority, to each one {{gender:their|his}} work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

R.34: It is like a man who goes on a trip. He leaves his house and puts his servants in charge of it. He gives each one a job to do. He tells the one who guards the door to stay awake and keep watch.

decisions.choice: slaves: household slaves who ran the house for their owner
decisions.reason: The word means slaves, people owned by their master. In a large household some were trusted with the running of the house.

decisions.choice: the authority: charge of the house while the owner was away
alternatives: power over the other slaves only
decisions.reason: He hands over the running of his house, with work for each one.

decisions.choice: the doorkeeper: the slave who guarded the door and let people in
decisions.reason: His task is to stay awake and open when the owner returns.

decisions.choice: like: a comparison with no main verb
decisions.reason: The sentence begins a comparison and leaves it unfinished. Its point is drawn in the command that follows (13:35).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: He leaves ... puts ... orders (present tense)
decisions.reason: Balanced tells the comparison in the present, as one tells an example.

records.source: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ κύριος τῆς οἰκίας ἔρχεται, ἢ ὀψὲ ἢ μεσονύκτιον ἢ ἀλεκτοροφωνίας ἢ πρωΐ, μὴ ἐλθὼν ἐξαίφνης εὕρῃ ὑμᾶς καθεύδοντας·
records.gloss: Watch therefore, not you know for when the lord of the house comes, either at evening or at midnight or at rooster-crowing or early, \v 36 lest having come suddenly he find you sleeping.
pieces: So keep watch, since you cannot know when the master of the house is coming: in the evening, at midnight, at the crowing of the rooster, or at dawn.
Otherwise he may arrive suddenly and find you asleep.

L.35: Keep watch therefore, for you do not know when the lord of the house is coming, whether in the evening, or at midnight, or at rooster-crow, or early in the morning,
L.36: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

R.35: So stay awake! You do not know when the owner of the house will come back. It might be in the evening or at midnight. It might be when the rooster crows in the dark, or early in the morning.
R.36: If he comes suddenly, do not let him find you sleeping.

decisions.choice: evening, midnight, rooster-crow, early morning: the four watches of the night
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches of about three hours each, from about six in the evening to six in the morning. The owner may come in any of them.

decisions.choice: the lord of the house: the master and owner
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "Lord". In the comparison he is the owner, and he stands for Jesus, whose return the disciples must wait for.

decisions.choice: the four watches: the same times come in the story of Jesus' last night
decisions.reason: Evening (14:17), the disciples sleeping in the night (14:37-41), the rooster crowing (14:72), and early morning (15:1). Mark may intend his readers to notice.

decisions.choice: lest he find you sleeping: the reason to keep watch
decisions.reason: The danger is being found asleep when the master comes.

decisions.choice: lord (L); master (B); owner (R)
decisions.reason: In the comparison the word is lowercase, since it names the owner of the house. Literal keeps the word that can also mean Lord.

records.source: ὃ δὲ ὑμῖν λέγω πᾶσιν λέγω· γρηγορεῖτε.
records.gloss: What now to you I say, to all I say, keep watch.
pieces: What I tell you, I tell everyone: Keep watch!"

L.37: And what I say to you, I say to all: keep watch."

R.37: What I am telling you, I am telling everyone: Stay awake!"

decisions.choice: all: everyone, not just the four
decisions.reason: The speech was given to four disciples (13:3), but the warning is for all who follow Jesus.

decisions.choice: keep watch: a present command, keep on watching
decisions.reason: The speech ends with the same command as 13:35: stay watchful.

decisions.choice: tell (B); am telling (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "tell" for this kind of saying.
